<reason>Both sides were strong, but CON built the cleaner decision path. Its opening distinction — disclose the standard, not the detection machinery — organized the whole debate, and it then used PRO's own concessions to shrink the motion round by round. The decisive sequence was CON's A1 in Rebuttal 2: once PRO adopted asymmetric disclosure (workers get "materiality," regulators get the specification confidentially), CON showed that PRO's worker is *also* fired at a threshold she never saw, so the worker-facing half of the motion collapses into notice laws CON already accepts, leaving only the standing universal regulator filing — which CON attacked convincingly on dynamism (perma-stale snapshot vs version-by-version obligation) and on centralized exposure ("scalpel versus a warehouse of keys," a fair answer to PRO's discovery-exposure turn). PRO landed real hits: the circularity charge against litigation ("discovery follows a claim"), the "if secrecy is what keeps the proxy honest, the proxy never measured what it claimed" turn, and the pattern argument that only a regulator can see disparate outcomes across workers. CON conceded the pattern point's truth and answered only with complaint-triggered investigation, which leaves some residue for PRO, and CON never answered PRO's point that secrecy does not stop gaming but merely rations accurate gaming. PRO also left CON's small-firm-threshold contradiction jab unanswered, and two PRO turns were clipped, costing it the ends of its opening and second rebuttal. Net: CON answered the most important pressure more squarely and made the final choice easier to adjudicate ("everything PRO values arrives on trigger; the motion demands it standing and universal").</reason>
<best_rebuttal>CON's A1 in Rebuttal 2, turning PRO's asymmetric-disclosure answer against it: since PRO's own design gives workers only "materiality" and never the threshold, PRO's worker is also fired by a number she never saw — leaving PRO's marginal gain over already-conceded notice laws to be just the regulator repository, which CON then attacked on dynamism and breach risk.</best_rebuttal>
